title: Ops sync: evaluation gate & rollback playbook - Oakridge Capital
summary: Weekly POC sync to review last week's quality regressions, decide on an evaluation gate for the pilot, and agree rollback/fallback playbook. SE reviewed the anomaly (tokenization mismatch leading to score drop), customer to provide labeled failures. Agreed on short-term mitigation: pin to current quantized model + increase KV cache TTL; longer-term: run 48-hour dedicated throughput/latency bench. Next meeting focused on security checklist + labeled examples review.
topics: recent regression incident and root-cause hypothesis
data retention and audit logs for compliance

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-01 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Recording: yes
Notes: live mic, occasional overlaps
---
[00:00] Maya Chen: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, Lucas is here from our SE team, and we wanted to go over the regression you flagged last week and make a call on the evaluation gate for the pilot.
[00:08] Ravi Patel: hey Maya, uh thanks. we got a couple folks here, jen couldn't make it but Elena and Jorge are on.
[00:12] Elena Morris: hi, yeah sorry ran over on another call.
[00:15] Lucas Ortiz: quick agenda, we'll recap the incident, show a short repro, share the hypothesis, then discuss short term mitigation and the rollback playbook.
[00:22] Jorge Alvarez: sounds good, we mainly want to know how risky it is to keep rolling and what the rollback looks like.
[00:28] Maya Chen: perfect. Lucas, you want to take the incident recap?
[00:31] Lucas Ortiz: yeah. so last Tuesday at about 18:13 UTC we started seeing an uptick in false rejections on income-doc classification prompts. score down approx 9 points on the quality scorecard, which crossed your alert threshold. we reproduced the failure on our side with your prompt set A_v3 and the short form edge cases.
[00:48] Lucas Ortiz: initial guess is tokenization/quantization interaction — basically certain punctuation combos are producing off-by-one tokenization and then the KV-cache warm path is hitting a mismatch; on the quantized model path that amplifies and you get the wrong classification. it's a bit noisy, hypothesis still early.
[01:08] Elena Morris: hmm, that sounds plausible. we did change the preprocessor two weeks ago to normalize curly quotes, could that interact?
[01:15] Lucas Ortiz: yes — normalizers can change token boundaries. also we rolled a different quantization profile on Friday to reduce memory footprint. in isolation both are fine but together it can create these edgecases.
[01:25] Ravi Patel: can you explain, sorry, "KV cache warm path" — what does that mean in practice?
[01:30] Maya Chen: sure. roughly, when a session is continuing tokens are cached. if there's a token mismatch the runtime takes a different code path to reconstruct keys; sometimes that path uses slightly different ops for quantized weights. so it's a rare path but when it hits the score changes.
[01:46] Jorge Alvarez: so the real question — is this a platform bug or a config mismatch on our side?
[01:50] Lucas Ortiz: our current leaning is config + model profile interaction — not a critical platform bug. but we want to be conservative about the pilot gate.
[01:58] Maya Chen: important — we don't want to over-assume. we ran a quick repro that shows the issue on our hosted cluster and on a small dedicated pool; that suggests it's not purely infra.
[02:09] Elena Morris: we noticed some false positives in guardrails too; things that should be allowed are being blocked. is that related?
[02:15] Lucas Ortiz: could be related if the token boundary shifts. guardrail classifiers are sensitive to token sequences. also sometimes the safety model version mismatch can introduce higher false positives.
[02:25] Maya Chen: ok so short-term options: 1) pin current stable quantized model (roll back quant profile) for the pilot while we debug; 2) increase KV cache TTL to reduce warm path hits; 3) tweak preprocessor to a safer normalizer; 4) run a targeted bench on Dedicated to validate. these can be combined.
[02:40] Ravi Patel: cost will matter — pinning to older quant profile raises memory and cost, how much?
[02:45] Lucas Ortiz: ballpark: 8–12% memory and 6–9% cost increase for the profile we rolled away from. but Dedicated burst options can help.
[02:54] Jorge Alvarez: and the evaluation gate — are we saying anything that crosses the scorecard triggers a rollback? what's the SOP?
[02:59] Maya Chen: we recommend a decision gate: if score drops >5 points on the weekly scorecard and false positive rate increase >3% on guardrails for two consecutive runs, we hit the gate. then we can either do a canary rollback (reserve a small % of traffic to previous model) or full rollback. we usually prefer canary first.
[03:17] Elena Morris: can we automate that? the weekly cadence is fine but we'd prefer automated alerts and a one-click rollback.
[03:23] Lucas Ortiz: yes - Redwood Console supports canary and automatic revert policies. we can configure the threshold and a 1-click revert from the dashboard. I'll share the config template.
[03:32] Ravi Patel: about telemetry — we need audit logs for regulatory reasons, and retention for six months. do you support per-customer audit export?
[03:38] Maya Chen: yes, Private and Dedicated modes ship audit logs; Hosted API can forward logs to your S3 with KMS encryption and we have an export path. SOC2 docs in folder.
[03:48] Jorge Alvarez: great. also procurement will ask about contract SLAs — what's the SLA on latency for Dedicated?
[03:53] Lucas Ortiz: typical 95th P99 targets depend on instance type; we'll include a bench with 95/99 latencies in the report we share. that bench is one of the next steps.
[04:01] Elena Morris: quick question — is the regression reproducible with our exact data, or only with a synthesized snippet?
[04:06] Lucas Ortiz: reproducible with your subset of 600 prompts you shared; but frequency increases when the curly-quote normalizer is enabled.
[04:12] Ravi Patel: ok, operationally we want a playbook that lists: detect -> canary rollback -> pin model -> notify stakeholders -> run deeper root-cause. can you put that in a runbook?
[04:21] Maya Chen: yes we'll draft a short runbook with flow diagrams. Lucas will add the console settings.
[04:25] Lucas Ortiz: also, for now we suggest a temporary guardrail loosen on those specific rule IDs you flagged; that reduces false positives while we fix tokenization. but that increases risk surface so it's targeted change only.
[04:36] Jorge Alvarez: do we have examples of false positive messages? Elena?
[04:39] Elena Morris: yeah i'll upload three examples into the shared drive and mark why they should pass.
[04:43] Maya Chen: perfect. two more items: security deep-dive next week and pricing update for burst/dedicated.
[04:50] Ravi Patel: procurement wants pricing for reserved capacity and burst. also can you show what preemptable GPU option looks like in cost?
[04:56] Lucas Ortiz: yes, Maya and I will prepare a pricing sheet with a few scenarios.
[05:00] [Interruption - brief phone beep]
[05:05] Jorge Alvarez: last thing on rollback — how long does it take to revert to previous model in worst case?
[05:09] Lucas Ortiz: with canary, config flip is seconds, rollout across all nodes is minutes depending on batch size; full rollback can be 5–15 minutes for large fleets.
[05:17] Elena Morris: acceptable.
[05:19] Maya Chen: ok let's recap action items quickly: Lucas bench + console config, Maya pricing & SOC2 links, Elena upload labeled cases, Ravi confirm procurement contacts. schedule security deep-dive.
[05:31] Ravi Patel: agreed. thanks all.
[05:34] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the bench results and the runbook.
[05:38] [00:45] Meeting end
